segmentation.text: walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;

elements.justification: As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: rel.occupies of a st.sidewalk while moving.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: a st.obstruction within the encounter reach (st.region_geometry) while on the sidewalk.
As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: nearest atoms with a gap.
'may proceed': on the highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way), off every sidewalk (rel.occupies).
'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in that situation.
'return to the sidewalk': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps a st.sidewalk again (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.convention: Return time (a few steps at the HCM design walking speed): once no obstruction lies within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of the pedestrian (st.region_geometry distance to every st.obstruction), the return to the sidewalk is made within p.sidewalk_return_time.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; the duty to return to the sidewalk is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

applicability: As NRS_484B_297_6_o1: x is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian); for a sidewalk w (st.sidewalk) and a highway h (st.highway) with st.on_way w h, x occupies h and no sidewalk at this observation and has done so at every observation since an observation at which x occupied w, was moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) and was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of an obstruction (st.obstruction); and at this observation no obstruction lies within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x (x has passed it).
obligation: Within p.sidewalk_return_time ahead (a .time window), x occupies a sidewalk (rel.occupies x w2, w2 of kind st.sidewalk) at some observation.

narrowings.why: 'to move around such an obstruction' is read through leaving the sidewalk where the obstruction was encountered and staying off it since.

'as soon as practicable' is read as one fixed return time counted from the observations at which no obstruction is within reach; whether the sidewalk beside the pedestrian is passable there is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x leaves sidewalk w at a st.obstruction of kind excavation, walks past it on the roadway, and keeps walking on the roadway for 30 s with no obstruction within 5 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x leaves w at the excavation, passes it, and is back on w 2 s after the excavation is beyond the encounter reach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x walks on sidewalk w and never leaves it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.region_geometry is absent from the source.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
param_proposals.convention: Encounter reach: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to an obstruction within which the pedestrian has come up against it.
param_proposals.source: HCM pedestrian body ellipse and shy distance to fixed objects

param_proposals.name: p.sidewalk_return_time
param_proposals.convention: Return time: the time after a pedestrian has passed an obstruction within which a return to the sidewalk counts as made as soon as practicable; a few walking steps at the design walking speed.

gaps.proposal: st.impassable_section | a stretch of a sidewalk, or of the ground between a sidewalk and the roadway, that a pedestrian cannot traverse because its surface is missing or blocked, carried as a region with a boundary and the way it lies on; decides where a pedestrian may leave the sidewalk and where it may travel | general
